mechanism: coins-view-db-erase-all-coins (src/storage/coins-view.lisp:234) iterates the coins LevelDB and deletes only keys whose first byte is +db-prefix-coin+ (#x43 'C'); the best-block key is +db-prefix-best-block+ (#x42 'B', src/storage/coins-view.lisp:31,41) and therefore SURVIVES the wipe, and coins-view-cache-wipe (src/storage/coins-view-cache.lisp:324) only clrhashes the cache on top of it. do-reindex-chainstate (src/node/reindex.lisp:50-61) rewinds chainstate.dat to genesis and saves it with the in-transition marker BEFORE the wipe, and the first %flush-chainstate only fires once the replay cache reaches large-coins-cache-threshold of *coins-cache-budget-bytes* (450 MiB default, so ~405 MiB of rebuilt coins; src/node/flush.lisp:23,33-38, src/node/reindex.lisp:86-88). Every crash inside that window -- the whole LevelDB wipe plus the first several hundred MiB of replay -- leaves genesis+marker in chainstate.dat over a coins DB that is empty but still names the pre-reindex tip. On the next ordinary start, %init-recover-chain runs recover-inconsistent-chainstate's genesis branch (src/node/recovery.lisp:131-151), which does the right thing: re-wipe, clear the marker, stay at genesis. Then %init-services runs reconcile-coins-db-best-block UNCONDITIONALLY (src/node/init.lisp:864 -> src/node/recovery.lisp:3-63), reads the surviving pointer, finds that block in the index, and moves chainstate.dat FORWARD to the pre-reindex tip, logging 'Recovered'. Core cannot reach this state: InitCoinsDB is opened with should_wipe=options.wipe_chainstate_db (refs/bitcoin/src/node/chainstate.cpp:93) which is a leveldb::DestroyDB of the whole database (refs/bitcoin/src/dbwrapper.cpp:39-41,233), and is_coinsview_empty() is 'wipe_chainstate_db || CoinsTip().GetBestBlock().IsNull()' (chainstate.cpp:69-70), so LoadChainTip is SKIPPED and the chain stays at genesis; DB_BEST_BLOCK also lives inside the coin batch (refs/bitcoin/src/txdb.cpp:128,159). Core needs no persisted reindex-chainstate flag because an empty coins DB is self-describing; ours has a marker (in-transition) and honours it, and then overrides it.
consequence: Executed through the real bl:start-node path on a regtest datadir: after the simulated crash the node starts cleanly and reports height 8 at the pre-reindex tip with an EMPTY UTXO set (utxo-count 0, utxo-amount 0), and the operator's log says 'Chainstate recovery: interrupted reindex-chainstate; UTXO set reset to empty at genesis' immediately followed by 'UTXO set is at height 8 ... but chainstate.dat records tip height 0' and 'Recovered: chainstate.dat moved to the UTXO set's own block'. So the node serves a wrong chainstate as valid and calls it a successful recovery -- every UTXO-set RPC (gettxoutsetinfo, scantxoutset, wallet balances) answers for an empty set at that height. Second half, measured separately: the honest chain is NOT poisoned on the straight-line tip-extension path -- activate-block case 1 (src/validation/block.lisp:4208-4222) returns :missing-input WITHOUT calling %mark-block-subtree-invalid, so the next real block stayed :header-valid and the node merely stalls (handle-validation-failure, 3 attempts then silent). It IS poisoned on the REORG path: a competing fork with more work (the shape of any ordinary 1-block reorg) reaches activate-block case 2 -> perform-reorg -> %reorg-connect, whose :missing-input IS on *deterministic-invalid-block-errors* (src/validation/block.lisp:3134-3141) and calls %mark-block-subtree-invalid (src/validation/block.lisp:3522-3523). Executed: both fork blocks came back :INVALID, the marks SURVIVED a clean shutdown and restart, and a SECOND -reindex-chainstate rebuilt the UTXO set correctly (8 coins) while leaving both blocks :INVALID -- so the heavier honest chain is permanently rejected and only a per-hash reconsiderblock can undo it, with nothing in the log telling the operator to. Both halves of the S1 bar are met; the S2 escapes do not apply (the restart does not refuse, and a second reindex does not heal the marks).
evidence: Probes under build/ga11/ (git-ignored) loaded into BITCOIN-LISP.TESTS, driven with cl-workbench repl eval on the project container; a regtest datadir built and torn down entirely through bl:start-node / bl:stop-node, with the crash simulated by closing the coins LevelDB and releasing the datadir lock WITHOUT any flush (bl.store:close-chainstate-coins-view + unlock-data-directory), which is exactly what a killed process leaves behind. (1) baseline clean restart -> (:HEIGHT 8 :POINTER 7fc0bde0... :UTXO-COUNT 10 :UTXO-AMOUNT 40200000000). (2) reindex prefix only (update-chain-tip genesis / save-state :in-transition t / coins-view-cache-wipe): erased 10 coins, and the state read back (:HEIGHT 0 :TIP 0f9188f1<genesis> :POINTER 7fc0bde0... :UTXO-COUNT 0) -- the pointer survived the wipe. (3) ordinary bl:start-node restart, no flags -> (:HEIGHT 8 :TIP 7fc0bde0... :POINTER 7fc0bde0... :UTXO-COUNT 0 :UTXO-AMOUNT 0); node.log lines: '[warning] Chainstate recovery: interrupted reindex-chainstate; UTXO set reset to empty at genesis (chain will re-sync)' then '[warning] UTXO set is at height 8 (7fc0bde0...) but chainstate.dat records tip height 0; a reorg or flush was interrupted' then '[warning] Recovered: chainstate.dat moved to the UTXO set's own block' then 'Node started successfully'. (4) next real block at tip+1 (a block that spends a pre-wipe coin, built with generateblock submit=false while the node was healthy): delivered through bl.net::process-headers + process-received-block -> NIL, log '[warning] MISSING-INPUT: height=9 prev-txid=a1a1..:0' + '[error] Block 9 validation failed: MISSING-INPUT (attempt 1/3)', and the block-index status stayed :HEADER-VALID (NOT poisoned). (5) competing fork F8 (sibling of block 8, spends another pre-wipe coin) + F9, hand-built and PoW-ground, delivered the same way: log 'REORG: old tip height 8 -> fork at 7 -> new tip height 8', 'MISSING-INPUT: height=8 prev-txid=b2b2..:0', 'REORG ABORTED at height 8: fork block failed validation (MISSING-INPUT). Rolling back to original chain.' and both F8 and F9 came back :INVALID. (6) persistence and remedy: after bl:stop-node + restart, F8 (:HEIGHT 8 :STATUS :INVALID) and F9 (:HEIGHT 9 :STATUS :INVALID); after a second bl:start-node :reindex-chainstate t the UTXO set was rebuilt (:UTXO-COUNT 8 :UTXO-AMOUNT 40000000000) but F8 and F9 were STILL :INVALID. fix_shape: Do not implement here. Three layers, Core-faithful, smallest first. (a) Wipe the pointer WITH the coins: coins-view-db-erase-all-coins should erase the best-block key in the same final synced batch as the coins (Core's -reindex-chainstate destroys the whole LevelDB, and CCoinsViewDB::BatchWrite erases and rewrites DB_BEST_BLOCK inside the coin batch, txdb.cpp:128,159); an emptied coins DB must never name a block. Keep the migration marker ('M') exempt, or give the wipe an explicit keep-list rather than a keep-everything-not-'C' rule, and clear the cache's own best-block alongside it. (b) Make reconcile-coins-db-best-block refuse to move the tip FORWARD onto an empty coins view -- Core's is_coinsview_empty gate (chainstate.cpp:69-70) is exactly 'wipe requested OR GetBestBlock().IsNull()', and LoadChainTip is skipped under it; ours should treat 'pointer names block X but the view holds no coins' as the empty case, stay where recover-inconsistent-chainstate left it, and log that a rebuild is needed rather than logging 'Recovered'. (c) Order the two recoveries so the later one cannot silently undo the earlier: today %init-recover-chain resolves the interrupted reindex correctly and %init-services (init.lisp:864) reverses it a few steps later, so the reconcile should be told a chainstate was just reset by the genesis branch and skip it -- or, closer to Core, persist a reindex-chainstate-in-progress marker (Core's own -reindex flag lives in the block tree DB) so a restart resumes the rebuild instead of re-deriving the tip. Separately, whatever the fix, the persisted :invalid marks that this state can already have produced are not cleared by -reindex-chainstate; a fix should say how an affected node recovers (reconsiderblock, or clearing BLOCK_FAILED on a chainstate rebuild the way Core's full -reindex does).
